summary: Scale structure and the standards of gradable adjectives, after Kennedy and McNally. The endpoints of the four scale types; the antonym test (39); the 'half' tests (41)-(42); the comparative tests (43); and separating examples for relative adjectives (40), (44).

sources.citation: Kennedy, C. & McNally, L. (2005). Scale structure, degree modification, and the semantics of gradable predicates. Language 81(2): 345-381.

theorems.name: endpoints
theorems.source_claim: K1. (23): only the closed ends have endpoints.

theorems.name: absolute_antonyms
theorems.source_claim: K2. (39) p. 359: "The door is not open |= The door is closed", and the same with the adjectives exchanged.

theorems.name: half_tests
theorems.source_claim: K3. (41) p. 360: "half dead |= not dead"; (42): "half open |= open".

theorems.name: comparative_tests
theorems.source_claim: K4. (43a) p. 360: "wetter than the countertop |= wet", for a minimum standard; (43b): "drier than the countertop |= the countertop is not dry", for a maximum standard.

theorems.name: half_is_midpoint
theorems.source_claim: K5. (21) p. 353: the degree of "half" is the midpoint.

theorems.name: the_doors
theorems.source_claim: "open" has a minimum standard and "closed", its antonym, a maximum one. The door that is half open is open and is not closed; the shut door is closed and is not open.

theorems.name: zone_of_indifference
theorems.source_claim: Separating example 1. (40) p. 359: "not large" does not entail "small". With a standard of 2/3 for "large" and 2/3 for its antonym, the door of size 1/2 is neither.

theorems.name: comparative_without_positive
theorems.source_claim: Separating examples 2 and 3. (44) p. 360: with a relative standard, the comparative entails neither the positive form nor its negation.

theorems.name: comparative_with_positive
theorems.source_claim: stated in the file; see its header

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
Degrees are rational numbers and the four scales are the four intervals between 0 and 1.
The degree morpheme pos, degree modifiers and deverbal adjectives are not formalized.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. The entailment tests transpose directly once the three standards are given.
